Asynchronous Cross-Horizon Probabilistic Adaptation for Frozen Time-Series Foundation Models under Distribution Shift

Computational Intelligence & Time-Series Adaptation (CITA) Research Group
Collaborator Project C+ Addendum • Repository: https://github.com/vlqm2008/cita2027-phase2
ABSTRACT
Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) such as Chronos and Moirai exhibit strong zero-shot transfer capabilities across benchmark datasets. However, when deployed in non-stationary real-world environments, their frozen parameters cannot adapt to concept drift. Standard online adaptation techniques treat multi-horizon forecasting as a set of decoupled univariate streams, updating horizon-specific corrections only when ground truth realizes. Crucially, multi-step supervision arrives asynchronously: short-horizon outcomes (h=1) realize rapidly, whereas long-horizon outcomes (h=16) suffer from severe supervision delays.

In this work, we investigate whether a frozen probabilistic TSFM can exploit asynchronously arriving short-horizon feedback to adapt long-horizon predictive distributions prior to observing their delayed ground truth. We formulate three testable hypotheses: H1 (Cross-Horizon Transferability), H2 (Stale-Feedback Negative Transfer), and H3 (Overlap-Aware Stability). Across an audited prequential benchmark suite of 8 controlled distribution shifts and real-world financial return series (SPY and BTCUSDT), evaluated via Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS), Winkler interval score, paired circular block bootstrap (B=1000, b in {5, 10, 20}), and Holm-Bonferroni correction, we demonstrate that the proposed Unified Adapter (H_3) significantly outperforms independent horizon-wise EWMA (B_1) across all long horizons (h=4, 8, 16, Holm p < 0.001), reducing CRPS by up to 21.8%.

1. Problem Formulation and Mathematical Framework

Let {y_t}_{t=1}^T denote a non-stationary time series. At forecast origin t, a frozen foundation model ingests context x_t = (y_{t-L+1}, ..., y_t) and produces predictive samples over horizons H = {1, 4, 8, 16}:

S_{t,h}^{base} = { y_{t+h|t}^{(m)} }_{m=1}^M ~ p_M(y_{t+h} | x_t).

The true target y_{t+h} realizes strictly at timestamp tau = t + h. The feedback age is age(e, t) = t - (t_{orig} + h) >= 0. We apply an online affine distributional transformation:

y_{t+h|t}^{(m), adapted} = mu_{t+h|t}^{base} + w_h^T z_t + b_{t,h}^{local} + s_{t,h} * (y_{t+h|t}^{(m)} - mu_{t+h|t}^{base}),

where z_t in R^2 is a low-rank shared latent state, b_{t,h}^{local} is a local horizon offset, and s_{t,h} > 0 is the dispersion multiplier.

2. The Unified Cross-Horizon Adapter (H3)

The unified architecture combines three complementary mechanisms:

  • Cross-Horizon Transfer (H1): Projects residuals from early-maturing horizons into a shared 2D manifold.
  • Feedback-Age Attenuation (H2): Attenuates stale residuals via exponential decay: w_{age} = exp(-gamma * age) with gamma = 0.12 and drift gating.
  • Overlap Effective-Sample Normalization (H3): Scales the learning rate by the Kish effective sample size K_{eff} = (sum w_i)^2 / sum w_i^2 and bounds step norms.
Figure 1: Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) across forecasting horizons under severe Joint Shift. H3 Unified Adapter achieves growing advantages over frozen and independent baselines as horizon length increases.

4. Rigorous Statistical Significance & Ablation Studies

Paired Circular Block Bootstrap (B=1000, b in {5, 10, 20}) with Holm-Bonferroni correction (alpha = 0.05) establishes that:

  • Under Joint Shift, H3 vs. B1 achieves statistically significant CRPS reductions across all long horizons: h=4 (Holm p=0.0006), h=8 (p<0.0001), and h=16 (p=0.0010).
  • Under Variance Shift, H3 outperforms B1 with all three 95% bootstrap intervals strictly excluding zero and Holm p < 0.0001.
Figure 4: Systematic 4-panel ablation study: (a) Component breakdown confirms joint location-scale adaptation is indispensable; (b) Latent capacity shows d=2 is optimal; (c) Decay parameter gamma=0.12 balances damping; (d) Overlap factor beta=0.7 minimizes update variance.

5. Cross-Architecture Generalization (Chronos vs. Moirai)

Evaluating on both Amazon Chronos-T5-small and Salesforce Moirai-1.0-R-small reveals universal empirical principles:

  • Unregularized online mean tracking (B1) degrades performance universally across architectures on financial returns (0.0518 -> 0.0537 on Chronos; 0.0321 -> 0.0334 on Moirai).
  • Stabilized adaptation (H3) improves 80% interval Winkler scores by up to 24.4% over frozen Chronos and prevents runaway variance on Moirai.
Figure 5: Cross-architecture comparison on SPY and BTCUSDT validation sets confirming consistent stabilization benefits.

6. Conclusion and Reproducibility Statement

This project provides the first comprehensive empirical characterization of asynchronous multi-horizon probabilistic adaptation for frozen TSFMs. All experiments, unit tests, and figures are 100% reproducible via: 

python scripts/run_all_phases.py
